C1.object: Disney's Sing-Along Songs: Happy Haunting - Party at Disneyland!
C1.source_join: The Spooky Scary Skeletons number mixes the Andrew Gold song with scenes from Disney's 1929 The Skeleton Dance, alongside additional material.

D1.object: 2010 YouTube pairing of The Skeleton Dance with Spooky Scary Skeletons
D1.source_join: The 1929 Disney cartoon is paired with Andrew Gold's song; later reference sources identify the clip's characters as a persistent part of the meme.

features: Spooky Scary Skeletons used as a background track for skeleton-themed memes
2013 Living Tombstone remix amplifies dance/electronic circulation
exact Disney footage becomes optional rather than mandatory
skeleton imagery functions as a general seasonal marker beyond the original Disney frames

key_finding.statement: The internet association between Andrew Gold's song and Disney's 1929 skeleton animation has a pre-internet official Disney precursor in the 1998 Sing-Along Songs release.
key_finding.effect: The C->D lineage for the exact visual source is stronger than a family-level resemblance model: exact 1929 footage was deliberately recombined before the viral YouTube phase.

D1_direct_source_reuse.note: Ranges are preregistered estimates because exact edited shot coverage varies by version; visual form is retained through direct footage reuse while the soundtrack/platform/function changes.

D2_D3_diffuse_family.rule: Do not assign a single LRS vector to the entire Spooky/Spooktober ecosystem. Sample direct Disney GIFs, non-Disney skeleton memes, song-only uses, and captioned secondary-attribution examples separately.

C1929_to_C1_1998.basis: documented reuse of scenes from The Skeleton Dance in the 1998 Disney sing-along number

C1929_to_D1_2010.basis: the 2010 online video uses the exact 1929 cartoon as visual source

C1_1998_to_D1_2010_specific_remake_inten.basis: later histories describe the online version as recreating the earlier Disney pairing; creator-intent archival proof has not been independently recovered here

C_to_D2_D3_general_skeleton_culture.rule: Direct Disney-footage descendants can score high LES; generic skeleton memes, Spooktober images, and song-only uses require independent lineage analysis.

B_HOLBEIN_TO_C_DISNEY.boundary: This gate does not upgrade the Holbein->Disney archival lineage.

operator_analysis.new_mechanism: A cultural form can become more transmissible not by losing all structure, but by preserving a highly recognizable visual/audio nucleus while making surrounding context replaceable.

supported_examples: Spooky/Spooktober memes can be paired with intentionally non-frightening material
skeleton imagery and the song are reused as generic October/Halloween markers
individual depression-themed skeleton examples exist in meme galleries
secondary_attribution.boundary: Do not claim that burnout, depression, work anxiety, or rave culture is the canonical meaning of the meme without corpus-level evidence.

hypothesis_effect.important_refinement: C->D1 is not semantic collapse like B->C. It is direct formal retention plus platform and soundtrack recombination. The stronger semantic collapse occurs earlier at B->C; later digital transmission exploits the already-autonomous comic skeleton form.

epistemic_firewall: Exact visual reuse in D1 does not prove that every later skeleton meme descends from The Skeleton Dance.
A shared skeleton motif is not sufficient for lineage.
Spooktober is a broader seasonal internet category and must not be reduced to a single Disney-derived lineage.
Affective or psychological captions such as depression/burnout require object-level examples or corpus sampling before being treated as a stable semantic layer.
The direct visual C->D lineage does not solve the separate B->C Holbein-to-Disney provenance problem.
LRS similarity and LES lineage must remain independently scored.

targets: sample direct Skeleton Dance GIF/video descendants
sample non-Disney Spooky Scary Skeletons visual memes
sample secondary-caption reencodings such as work/depression/rave jokes
compute separate LRS distributions and LES classes rather than one average

source_receipts.claim: Video debut 1998; Spooky Scary Skeletons mixes neon puppets with scenes from the 1929 The Skeleton Dance.
2010 YouTube upload paired the 1929 Disney cartoon with the song; characters from the clip became a permanent part of the meme; meme recurs seasonally.
Spooktober spread as a broader seasonal meme category and later used Spooky Scary Skeletons in humorous mashups with non-frightening material.
Spooky Scary Skeletons became an unofficial soundtrack of Internet Halloween and participates in a broader cute-plus-scary spooky aesthetic.

canonical_seal: THE DIGITAL LINEAGE IS NOT MERELY A LOOKALIKE CHAIN. EXACT 1929 DISNEY FOOTAGE WAS RECOMBINED WITH SPOOKY SCARY SKELETONS IN OFFICIAL DISNEY HOME VIDEO BEFORE THE VIRAL INTERNET PHASE, THEN REMEDIATED ONLINE AND DIFFUSED INTO A BROADER SEASONAL MEME ECOLOGY. SCORE DIRECT FOOTAGE DESCENDANTS SEPARATELY FROM GENERIC SKELETON CULTURE. LRS IS NOT LES.
